parole.significato: A fortified, central complex found in various Russian cities.
parole.testo: Similar forms are attested, per Vasmer's Etymological Dictionary, in earlier German Kremelin and French Cremlin, which are theorized to come from Old East Slavic кремльнъ (kremlĭnŭ, “having a kremlin”), from кремль (kremlĭ), whence Russian кремль (kremlʹ).

parole.significato: a popular assembly in medieval Slavic countries.
parole.testo: From Old East Slavic вѣче (věče, “council”) or modern Russian ве́че (véče)

parole.significato: A medieval East Slavic actor or harlequin
parole.testo: Borrowed from Russian скоморох (skomorox), from Old East Slavic скоморохъ (skomoroxŭ), of unknown origin. Possibly from Ancient Greek σκώμμαρχος (skṓmmarkhos, “joke leader”) (σκῶμμα (skômma)+ἀρχός (arkhós)) or from Italian scaramuccia.
